title: The Golden Goose
author: Ellen C. Babbitt
summary: 金鹅每天送一根金羽毛，贪心的母亲却把它全拔光。
publicDomainBasis: Retold by Ellen C. Babbitt and published in 1922 by The Century Co. (pre-1923, public domain in the United States); Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time there was a Goose who had beautiful golden feathers. Not far away from this Goose lived a poor, a very poor woman, who had two daughters. The Goose saw that they had a hard time to get along and said he to himself:
paragraphs.zh: 从前有一只鹅，长着一身美丽的金羽毛。离这只鹅不远，住着一个很穷很穷的妇人，她有两个女儿。鹅见她们日子过得艰难，便对自己说：

paragraphs.en: "If I give them one after another of my golden feathers, the mother can sell them, and with the money they bring she and her daughters can then live in comfort."
paragraphs.zh: “如果我把金羽毛一根一根地给她们，母亲就可以拿去卖掉，用换来的钱，她和女儿们就能过上衣食无忧的日子了。”

paragraphs.en: So away the Goose flew to the poor woman's house.
Seeing the Goose, the woman said: "Why do you come here? We have nothing to give you."
paragraphs.zh: 妇人看见鹅，说：“你来这儿做什么？我们没什么可给你的。”

paragraphs.en: "But I have something to give you," said the Goose. "I will give my feathers, one by one, and you can sell them for enough so that you and your daughters can live in comfort."
paragraphs.zh: “可我有东西给你们，”鹅说，“我会一根一根地把羽毛给你们，你们拿去卖了，就够你和女儿们过舒服日子了。”

paragraphs.en: So saying the Goose gave her one of his feathers, and then flew away. From time to time he came back, each time leaving another feather.
paragraphs.zh: 说完，鹅给了她一根羽毛，就飞走了。此后它时不时回来，每次留下一根羽毛。

paragraphs.en: The mother and her daughters sold the beautiful feathers for enough money to keep them in comfort. But one day the mother said to her daughters: "Let us not trust this Goose. Some day he may fly away and never come back. Then we should be poor again. Let us get all of his feathers the very next time he comes."
paragraphs.zh: 母亲和女儿们把美丽的羽毛卖了，换来的钱足够她们过得舒舒服服。可有一天，母亲对女儿们说：“我们别信这只鹅。哪天它也许飞走就再也不回来了。那时我们又该受穷了。下次它一来，我们就把它的羽毛全拔下来。”

paragraphs.en: The daughters said: "This will hurt the Goose. We will not do such a thing."
paragraphs.zh: 女儿们说：“那会伤着鹅的。我们不做这种事。”

paragraphs.en: But the mother was greedy. The next time the Golden Goose came she took hold of him with both hands, and pulled out every one of his feathers.
paragraphs.zh: 可母亲贪心。金鹅下一次来时，她双手抓住它，把它身上的羽毛一根根全拔了下来。

paragraphs.en: Now the Golden Goose has strange feathers. If his feathers are plucked out against his wish, they no longer remain golden but turn white and are of no more value than chicken-feathers. The new ones that come in are not golden, but plain white.
paragraphs.zh: 金鹅的羽毛很奇特。若是违背它的意愿硬拔下来，羽毛就不再是金色，而会变成白色，跟鸡毛一样不值钱。新长出来的也不是金色，而是普普通通的白毛。

paragraphs.en: As time went on his feathers grew again, and then he flew away to his home and never came back again.
paragraphs.zh: 日子一天天过去，它的羽毛又长了出来，然后它飞回自己的家，再也没有回来。
